decision: Replace c2 with a longer, much stiffer two-cell/two-segment arm and a hierarchical 3+3 tendon topology: three tendons anchor after the proximal segment and three continue through both segments. This preserves six independent channels while enabling proximal/distal curvature cancellation needed because the three targets have substantially different chord lengths. Immediately query zero-state mechanics to verify geometry, gravity bias, and channel authority before spending another rollout.
evidence: The first c2 rollout showed severe over-actuation: 2.5–3.2 N paired commands folded the arm to x near zero, with 0.10–0.15 m stroke and 0.28–0.49 m/s tendon speed. Earlier c2 mechanics predicted about +112 m/s^2 vertical acceleration per 1 N symmetric pair, so gravity compensation was only about 0.09 N per tendon, not several newtons. The observed 12 generalized coordinates also supported large oscillatory deformation. Targets measured from the 0.15 m mount have chord lengths about 0.302 m (central), 0.289 m (positive), and 0.278 m (negative), motivating an approximately 0.316 m straight reach plus independently controllable opposing segment bends. Two one-cell segments, 4 MPa maximum-size tubes, and 23 mm routing radius are expected to reduce low-frequency folding while retaining enough curvature under the 8 N limit.

decision: Replace c4 with a lighter, moderately compliant two-link tube design c5 and immediately test all three required conditions using mode-aware two-stage tension commands. c4's measured stiffness and force map show that its distal upward equilibrium authority is inadequate: even tendon 3 at 8 N supplies only -0.159 Nm against 0.048 Nm gravity and 0.495 Nm/rad distal stiffness, limiting distal deflection to about -0.22 rad, whereas the central target's simultaneous 23 mm axial shortening and 65 mm rise requires substantially larger differential curvature. Tube sections lower bending stiffness and gravity while retaining adequate section clearance. The commands exploit measured c4 signs: tendon 3 drives positive y and positive z, tendon 4 cancels y without materially changing z, and root-only tendon 2 adjusts root curvature. Splitting each final command into half-amplitude and full-amplitude stages approximately one half-period apart is expected to reduce residual vibration during the 0.54-0.60 s hold.
evidence: At c4's zero state the tip is [0.318,0,0.15]. Measured stiffnesses are [0.402,0.402,0.495,0.495] Nm/rad, gravity bias is [-0.223,0,-0.048,0] Nm, and tendon 3 supplies [-0.0199,+0.0115,-0.0199,+0.0115] Nm/N. Its acceleration map confirms tendon 3 drives +y/+z, tendon 4 strongly drives -y with negligible z, and a 2:1 tendon-3:tendon-4 ratio approximately cancels lateral bending. The required targets span +65 mm z, +35 mm y/+35 mm z, and -40 mm y/-15 mm z, so all three measured actuation directions are needed and must be tested on the same candidate.

Evaluate all three original required conditions in the same batch. Use smooth multi-stage ramps rather than discontinuous steps, with the measured c4 tendon directions and moderate amplitudes adjusted for c6's lower tube stiffness; this should produce the required planar and lateral bends while reducing excitation before the holding window.

Earlier c4 mechanics measured an initial tip [0.318,0,0.15], stiffness [0.402,0.402,0.495,0.495] Nm/rad, gravity bias [-0.223,0,-0.048,0] Nm, and showed that full-span tendon 3 drives +y/+z while tendon 4 drives -y with little z; an approximately 2:1 tendon-3:tendon-4 ratio cancels lateral motion. The c6 tube sections have substantially lower EI than c4, so commands are reduced and ramped. Four cells per segment should provide a full-rank distributed bending basis while remaining computationally modest.
